source.section: Number of Factors and Sum of all Factors

problem.text: Find the greatest power of $5$ that divides $156!$.

steps.title: Where to start: count the factors of $5$ in the product
steps.body: $156! = 1\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdots 156$, so the $5$s come only from the multiples of $5$ in that list. Legendre's formula organizes the count: first count every multiple of $5$ once.

your_turn.prompt: How many multiples of $5$ are there from $1$ to $156$?

steps.title: Count the extra $5$s
steps.body:
Careful: a number like $25 = 5^2$ contributes two $5$s, and $125 = 5^3$ contributes three, but the first count gave each of them only one. So add one more for each multiple of $25$, and one more again for each multiple of $125$.
$$\left\lfloor \frac{156}{5} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \frac{156}{25} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \frac{156}{125} \right\rfloor + \left\lfloor \frac{156}{625} \right\rfloor$$

your_turn.answer: $6$, $1$ and $0$. Once a term is $0$ we can stop.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The number of $5$s in $156!$ is $31 + 6 + 1 + 0 = 38$. So the greatest power of $5$ that divides $156!$ is **$5^{38}$**.
